traits.build_notes: ALL TRAIT NUMBERS ARE ESTIMATES (position-specific means could not be read from full texts). Basis: elite men setters profiled 1.98-2.00 m with spike 345-363 cm and block 320-340 cm (Giannelli, Christenson - tall examples); professional men overall spike ~3.43 m / block ~3.27 m (cited from Palao 2014) and setters are generally shorter than hitters/middles, so typical elite setter set slightly lower. Elite women setters profiled 1.78-1.88 m, spike 303-313 cm, block 279-305 cm (Orro, Wolosz, Poulter); elite women overall ~1.82 m with ~2.34 m reach (Valades & Palao). Standing reach estimated as ~1.29-1.30 x stature. U16 girls: competitive (regional/national-pathway) setters estimated ~1.71 m; Serbian U17 national-team mean ~1.77 m (all positions) and setters are shorter than hitters/middles in youth samples; club-level U16 setters will often be 1.62-1.70 m. Build: lean, athletic, usually lighter and shorter than middles/opposites, with lower squat strength and jump than hitters (Marques 2009; national-team data); long arms and strong fingers/wrists matter more than mass. Gear: regular team jersey (not the contrasting libero shirt), shorts (women: spandex), low-profile knee pads, court shoes; ankle braces and finger tape (buddy-taped fingers) are common on setters. Right-handed setter assumed; left-handed setters are mirrored.

techniques.name: Setter ready at target (pass in the air)
techniques.description: Setter has arrived at the target (right of centre, ~1 m off the net), feet already set with the right foot ahead and hips nearly square to the left antenna but slightly open to the court so the passer is in view (yaw ~100). Knees softly bent (~45-60 deg), trunk almost upright, chin lifted to track the incoming pass; hands are on their way up at chin/face height but not yet in the setting window.

Estimated: no study reports a full-body posture for this instant; knee/hip values chosen to match the set-contact posture below and anatomical leg geometry (FK-checked: both feet on the floor, back heel just lifted).

techniques.name: Front set - ball contact (standing)
techniques.description: Ball is caught in a window ~10-15 cm above and slightly in front of the forehead; thumbs point back toward the eyes, the hands are cocked back (wrists ~60-70 deg extended) and the elbows point out and forward at roughly chin height (forearms ~35-40 deg below horizontal from hand to elbow, elbows ~100 deg flexed). Body faces the left antenna with the right shoulder to the net, right foot ~18 cm ahead, knees softly bent (~40 front / ~55 back, back heel slightly lifted), trunk nearly vertical, eyes looking up through the hands.

techniques.name: Front set - release / follow-through
techniques.description: Legs and arms have extended together: arms finish pointing up and forward along the set trajectory toward the left antenna (shoulders ~150 deg flexed, elbows nearly straight ~15 deg), hands about shoulder-width apart and the wrists back to almost neutral (they flex during projection but do not pass neutral). Knees nearly straight (~20 deg), weight moving onto the front (right) foot, chin up following the ball.

Estimated from coaching cues ('extend elbows as the knees extend', 'freeze the hands toward the target') and the ISBS observation that the wrist returns toward but not past neutral.

techniques.name: Back set - ball contact
techniques.description: Looks almost identical to the front-set contact (disguise): same right-foot-forward stance facing the left antenna, but the ball is taken a little further back, more directly above the forehead/hairline, so the shoulders are slightly more flexed (~142 deg) and the head tilts back further. Trunk stays upright; elite setters avoid an early hip thrust or arch because blockers read it.

Estimated: back sets show greater head, trunk and shoulder angular displacement than front sets (per protocol-2026 review of Ridgway & Wilkerson) - applied here mainly in the release posture.

techniques.name: Back set - release / follow-through
techniques.description: Arms extend up and slightly back over the head (shoulders ~172 deg flexed on a trunk that is extending ~15 deg), hips pushed forward over the feet, upper back gently arched and head tipped back to watch the ball travel behind toward the right antenna. Knees nearly straight; back heel lifted. Keep the arch modest - Dunning-style coaching keeps the body neutral to disguise the set.
evidence: Volleyball Canada - Setting the C set, skill description - https://volleyball.ca/uploads/Development/Coach/Skills/One_page_desc./ADV_DEV/EN/Setting_the_C_set_for_e_module_skill_description.pdf

techniques.name: Jump set - ball contact
techniques.description: Setter jumps off both feet (feet close, right slightly ahead) facing the left antenna and contacts the ball on the way up or near the peak with the same high hand window above the forehead; arms are a little higher than in the standing set. Legs hang slightly flexed (hips ~15, knees ~30 deg) with the ankles plantarflexed after take-off; trunk upright.

techniques.name: Setter dump (left-hand attack on two)
techniques.description: Front-row setter jumps exactly as for a jump set, then at the last instant lets the right hand fall away and uses the LEFT hand (which sits on the court side of the ball) to push the ball over the net to the right and down. Left arm reaches high over the head (shoulder ~165 deg, elbow ~30 deg) with the wrist snapping down; chest and shoulders turn slightly toward the net and the trunk leans a little toward it.
evidence: Gold Medal Squared - setter dump (looks like a set until the last instant, then swiped over with the left hand) - https://goldmedalsquared.com/?p=7964

techniques.name: Setter release / penetration run from right back
techniques.description: Back-row setter releases from area 1 as soon as the serve is struck and sprints to the target with an athletic forward lean (~15 deg), arms swinging (not held up), head turned toward the passer. Snapshot shows the left foot pushing off on the toes while the right knee drives forward; the final steps (R-L-R) then convert into the set-ready stance.

techniques.name: Block ready - right-front setter at the net
techniques.description: Front-row setter stands square to the net in right front, feet about shoulder width, knees bent ~40 deg, trunk upright, hands up in front of the face at about forehead height with palms toward the net and elbows bent ~95 deg, eyes on the opposing setter/hitter.

techniques.name: Block jump - peak
techniques.description: At the top of the block jump the arms are extended up and forward over the net (shoulders ~160 deg, elbows almost straight), hands about a ball-width apart with the wrists firm and angled slightly down into the opponent court; trunk slightly piked (~10 deg) and the legs hang with hips and knees ~20 deg flexed, ankles plantarflexed.

Estimated: jump 0.45 m chosen so hand height matches typical setter block reach minus standing reach (see traits); joint angles estimated.

techniques.name: Block landing - initial contact
techniques.description: Setter lands from the block on the forefeet with knees only slightly flexed (~11 deg) and hips nearly straight at the instant of floor contact, arms still coming down in front of the head; the knees then flex further to absorb load. Teaching point: land with more knee flexion (low-flexion landings are linked to ACL risk).

techniques.name: Back-row defensive base (right back)
techniques.description: When in the back row the setter defends right back before releasing: medium athletic stance, feet a bit wider than shoulders with the right foot slightly ahead, knees ~65-70 deg, trunk leaning ~18 deg, hands relaxed in front at waist height, body angled toward the cross-court attacker.

techniques.name: Low dig - right-back defence (contact)
techniques.description: Low, wide platform dig in right back: knees ~95-100 deg, trunk leaning ~34 deg, arms straight and joined into a platform angled down toward the floor at knee-to-thigh height, wrists pointing down, head up watching the ball. Right (sideline) foot slightly ahead so the platform faces the middle of the court.

techniques.name: Forearm (bump) set from a low pass
techniques.description: When the pass is too low or far for hands, the setter faces the left antenna, drops into a medium stance (knees ~60-67 deg, trunk ~20 deg) and lifts the ball with a straight-armed platform at waist height, finishing with a gentle leg-driven upward follow-through.

Estimated from forearm-pass kinematics and setting footwork orientation (yaw 90 = facing the left antenna).

techniques.name: Attack coverage behind the hitter
techniques.description: After setting, the setter follows and crouches low behind the attacking hitter (here toward the left side, yaw ~45): wide stance, knees ~92-95 deg, trunk ~27 deg forward, arms low and in front with palms up ready to play a blocked ball, head tipped back to watch the block.
evidence: Ridgway & Hamilton - The Kinematics of Forearm Passing in Low Skilled and High Skilled Volleyball Players - https://ojs.ub.uni-konstanz.de/cpa/article/view/2336

Estimated: no study or manual examined here gave coverage angles; built from the low-defence posture with the head raised toward the block.

techniques.name: Transition off the net after blocking (front-row setter)
techniques.description: After landing from a block the right-front setter turns toward the court (pivoting on the right foot, yaw ~135) and steps off the net with the left foot to find the dig and move to the setting target, staying in a moderate crouch with arms swinging low.
evidence: Coaches Insider - Setting drills (setters sprint to the net from right back, middle back and left front, then set outside) - https://coachesinsider.com/volleyball/setting-drills-article/

Estimated: transition footwork described qualitatively only; angles are generic running/stepping values.

techniques.name: Standing float serve - toss with arm cocked
techniques.description: Right-handed setter serving from behind the end line: left foot ahead, weight on the back foot, chest turned slightly right; the left arm has lifted the ball up in front of the hitting shoulder (left shoulder ~150 deg, arm straight) while the right elbow is drawn high and back at about shoulder height with the hand behind the ear (bow-and-arrow).

techniques.name: Standing float serve - ball contact
techniques.description: Weight has shifted onto the front (left) foot with the right foot trailing on its toes; the hitting arm is high and in front of the right shoulder (shoulder ~160 deg flexed, elbow ~15 deg) and the wrist is firm/neutral for a no-spin punch; trunk square to the net, left arm pulled down in front of the body.

techniques.name: Jump float serve - ball contact
techniques.description: Many elite setters jump-float: after a short (2-3 step) approach and a low toss, ball is struck with a firm wrist just after the peak of a modest jump (~0.3 m), arm high in front of the hitting shoulder, trunk nearly square, legs slightly flexed with plantarflexed ankles.
